card: This pull request adds a Python multisig setup utility to contrib/multisig alongside functional test coverage. It guides coordinators and cosigners through wallet creation, BIP 87 key generation, cosigner key collection, descriptor assembly, verification, and descriptor import for both P2WSH and Taproot multisig schemes. Setting up multisig descriptor wallets currently requires manual descriptor assembly and awkward RPC workarounds for key validation and import. The author presents the tool as a working prototype for tracking issue #35645 to help shape downstream RPC and wallet improvements. It is self-contained in contrib and functional tests, carrying no external PR dependencies.
evidence: Part of tracking issue #35645 (Multisig Wizard tracking issue) and references discussions on #36143.
PR description notes the tool is intended to demonstrate the setup flow 'so that RPC and interface work is shaped by what that flow actually needs' (author claim).
problem: Setting up multisig descriptor wallets across participants currently requires manual key derivation, descriptor construction, and multiple RPC workarounds, such as substituting private keys to bypass importdescriptors restrictions and wrapping keys in pkh() expressions to validate them. Bitcoin Core lacks high-level tooling or structured RPC workflows to coordinate multisig key collection, descriptor verification, and import.

risk.why: Mistakes are confined to an external contrib helper script and a functional test, with no impact on consensus, wallet internals, or release binaries.

scope_notes: Self-contained script in contrib/multisig with functional test coverage; does not modify any C++ node or wallet source files.
summary: Adds a standalone Python multisig setup wizard in contrib/multisig and an accompanying functional test. The utility orchestrates the end-to-end setup flow for k-of-n descriptor wallets across coordinators and participants using existing RPCs. It supports BIP 87 key generation, cosigner key validation, and descriptor assembly for both P2WSH sortedmulti and Taproot MuSig2 with sortedmulti_a.
